data.gender_notes: Anastina is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Anastasia is derived from the Greek word anastasis, meaning resurrection. In the Bible, Anastasia is the name of a saint and a martyr who was a victim of persecution during the reign of Emperor Diocletian. She was a young girl who, along with her mother Justina and her brother Julian, was executed for refusing to renounce her faith in Christ. Her feast day is celebrated on December 22.
data.etymology: Anastina belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Resurrection.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Anastina total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_hebrew.name: אנאסטינה
in_hebrew.meaning: השם אנאסטינה נגזר מיוונית ופירושו תחיית המתים
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם אנאסטינה מקורו ביוונית ונגזר מהמילה 'אנאסטסיס' (ἀνάστασις), שפירושה תחיית המתים. שם זה הוא תופעה של שמות נוצריים שונים שמקורם ביוונית ומשמעותם קשורה לתחייתו של ישו. השם משקף את האמונה הנוצרית בתחיית המתים ובישועת הנפש.

in_greek.name: Αναστασία
in_greek.meaning: Το όνομα Αναστασία σημαίνει ανάσταση και νέα ζωή
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Αναστασία προέρχεται από την ελληνική λέξη 'ανάστασις' (ἀνάστασις), που σημαίνει ανάσταση ή επάνοδος στη ζωή. Στην παράδοση της Εκκλησίας, το όνομα συνδέεται με την Ανάσταση του Χριστού και συμβολίζει τη νίκη της ζωής έναντι του θανάτου. Η Αναστασία είναι ένα από τα πολλά ονόματα που έχουν δοθεί προς τιμή της χριστιανικής πίστης και παράδοσης.

data.cultural_impact: Anastasia has been an intriguing and beloved figure throughout history. She is known for her unwavering faith and courage in the face of persecution. Her name has been given to numerous saints and Blesseds in the Catholic Church, and she is venerated as a patron saint of hopeless causes, lost articles, and those who have been falsely accused. Her story has been serialized, dramatized, and even mythologized in various artistic and literary works, inspiring countless individuals and communities.
data.spiritual_significance: Anastasia's name is a powerful reminder of the resurrection and the hope that it brings. By bearing this name, individuals are called to embrace the courage and fortitude of Anastasia, to never compromise their faith, and to trust in the power of the resurrection to overcome even the greatest of trials.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Anastasia means "resurrection" in Greek. It symbolizes the hope and promise of new beginnings and the triumph of life over death. In Christianity, it is a reminder of the resurrection of Jesus Christ and the eternal life He offers to all believers.

historical_references.reference: Saint Anastasia of Sirmium, also known as Anastasia the Martyr, was a Christian saint venerated in the Eastern Orthodox, Roman Catholic, Anglican, and Lutheran Churches. She is best known for her martyrdom during the Diocletian Persecution in the late 3rd century AD.
historical_references.context: Anastasia was a Roman noblewoman who was martyred during the Diocletian Persecution for her refusal to recant her Christian faith.

historical_references.reference: Anastasia of Kiev, also known as Anastasia of the Cave, was a medieval Russian princess who lived in the 11th century AD. She is venerated as a saint in the Eastern Orthodox Church. According to legend, she lived as a hermit in a cave near the Holy Dormition Monastery in Kiev, where she was later discovered and venerated by the monks.
